name: MalruleLib
summary: 101 faulty procedures in school mathematics ("malrules"), each as code that works a problem wrongly step by step, with 4,991 generated problems and the wrong answer each gives: can a system tell which procedure a wrong answer came from?

license.note: MalruleLib Non-Commercial License: academic research, education, open-source projects and evaluating open-weight models are allowed, with attribution; commercial use and evaluating commercial or closed models are not; anything made from it carries the same terms.
license.terms: non-commercial; attribution; share-alike; no evaluating commercial or closed models

cite: Chen, X., Liu, N., & Sonkar, S. (2026). MalruleLib: Large-scale executable misconception reasoning with step traces for modeling student thinking in mathematics. arXiv:2601.03217. https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03217

fits.how: Its wrong answers are an outside test of anything that names the procedure behind one. The harness's own computed diagnosis (src/diagnose.js) is scored on it by evals/diagnosis/malrulelib.mjs, from a clone on your own computer.

connect.note: None of it is in this repository, which its license wouldn't allow under MIT. Clone it and run node evals/diagnosis/malrulelib.mjs malrulelib/data/raw_data.csv: no model is called.
